core_obligations: Reduce to finite transcendence degree (proof lines 19678-19683): if the transcendence degree is infinite the statement is clear; otherwise choose a tower L = L_r / L_{r-1} / ... / L_0 = K with each step of transcendence degree one, so that it suffices to prove the case r = 1.

Write L as a filtered colimit (proof lines 19683-19686): in the degree one case one writes L as the filtered colimit of its finite type K-subalgebras A_i, and the cited colimit lemma reduces the assertion to the bound cd(A_i) <= 1 + cd(K).

Apply the curve bound (proof lines 19686-19688): the required bound for the finite type K-algebras A_i of transcendence degree one over K is precisely the cited curve lemma, which completes the proof.
proof_roadmap: Split the extension into a tower of transcendence degree one steps and reduce to that case.
Express the field as a filtered colimit of finite type subalgebras and apply the colimit bound.
Conclude with the bound for curves over the base field.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a field extension L/K the cohomological dimension satisfies cd(L) <= cd(K) + trdeg_K(L) (statement lines 19672-19676). The proof (proof lines 19678-19689) reduces to transcendence degree one by a tower of extensions, writes the field as a filtered colimit of finite type K-subalgebras to invoke the colimit bound, and finishes with the curve bound. H2: a two-step reduction with two inputs, written out in full.
